articles.title: Service Changes on Rochdale Line Due to Planned Works
articles.excerpt: All tram services between Oldham and Rochdale will be suspended for nearly two weeks as part of major Metrolink engineering works, with a replacement bus service available for affected passengers.
articles.content_html:
All tram services between Oldham and Rochdale will be suspended for nearly two weeks as major engineering works are carried out on the Metrolink lines. The closure began on Monday, August 17, and will last until Friday, August 28, affecting all stops along the route, including Shaw, Newhey, and Milnrow.

The suspension follows a weekend of full closure for track renewal works, which are part of a £150 million upgrade to the Metrolink network, the largest in its history. Previously, similar closures occurred in July for the Eccles, Trafford Centre, and Altrincham lines, which were shut for three weeks as part of the ongoing improvements.

A replacement bus service will be available for passengers holding tram tickets during this period. Ian Davies, network director for Metrolink, expressed gratitude to passengers for their patience and noted that Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has been attentive to feedback regarding the reliability of replacement services.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and take advantage of the replacement bus service during the closure. Further updates on the progress of the works and any additional service changes will be communicated by TfGM as they arise.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting step-free access for passengers. Alternative routes are available for those travelling towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop has been out of service since 7:23pm on 16 August 2026 and will remain unavailable until further notice. This disruption affects accessibility for passengers using the tram service.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading away from Manchester can also use a ramp from Cromford Street and must cross the tracks to access the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption. Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and consider alternative routes if necessary.

For further information, visit the Transport for Greater Manchester website.

articles.title: Rochdale Hornets Secure First League Win Against Workington Town
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Hornets clinched their first league victory in seven matches with a 22-20 win over Workington Town at Fibrus Community Stadium on Sunday, thanks to a strong performance from Jamie Dallimore.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Hornets achieved a much-needed victory on Sunday, defeating Workington Town 22-20 at Fibrus Community Stadium. This win marks the Hornets' first league success in seven attempts, providing a significant boost to their campaign.

The match began positively for Rochdale, who took an early lead with a penalty goal from Max Flanagan. However, Workington quickly responded, scoring two tries to take a 14-6 lead. Despite this setback, the Hornets mounted a comeback, showcasing resilience and determination.

Jamie Dallimore played a pivotal role in the victory, scoring two crucial tries that helped turn the tide in favour of Rochdale. The Hornets' forwards, including Mark Ioane and Jordan Syme, contributed significantly to the team's performance, putting pressure on the Workington defence throughout the match.

Looking ahead, the Hornets will aim to build on this momentum in their upcoming fixtures, as they seek to improve their standing in the league. The victory not only boosts morale but also reinforces the team's potential as they continue their season.
